A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPARK work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, efficiency experiments, ablations and case studies, including multimodal results in Appendix C.3.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds branching diagnostics, numerical teacher-model comparisons and test-time branching results.

M1.justification: The training algorithm remains unchanged. Appendix C.5 adds spark-inference, which branches when <explore> appears during inference and selects continuations through majority voting, extending beyond the retained Pass@16 evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, Sokoban and EZPoints, including the same generalization splits. New analyses use existing coverage without introducing different tasks or environments.

E2.justification: V2 Table 16 adds an explicit baseline-inference control for the new spark-inference procedure. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged; newly discussed ARPO, FR3E and DeepSearch are not empirically evaluated.

E3.justification: New protocols include branching-factor tests at B=2,3,4, trigger-rate monitoring through training step 150, and conditional test-time branching with majority voting. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, model sizes and stated default training settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands investigation of the exploration mechanism: branching-factor sensitivity, trigger dynamics during training, SFT tag-position statistics, tag-renaming robustness and test-time branching utility. Table 10 also quantifies teacher sensitivity that v1 described only qualitatively.

E5.justification: Both retain the seed-0 evaluation statement and the same Wilcoxon analysis, including p=9.7e-4 and alpha=0.05. The statistical appendix moves from C.5 to C.6; no additional repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice appears.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial diagnostic results on branching sensitivity, trigger dynamics, tag positions and teacher effects. Table 16 additionally reports spark-inference scores of 98.4/71.9/78.8 versus baseline-inference's 96.9/69.5/75.8 on ALFWorld/ScienceWorld/WebShop. These are new inference-condition results, not corrected earlier scores.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8) and Appendix A's uncertainty definition and heuristic efficiency/sample-complexity arguments are retained. Changes to mathematical passages are punctuation and reflow, without new assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about selective branching, resource efficiency and generalization. The abstract's added code/checkpoint announcement changes access information.

C2.justification: V2 explains larger branching factors through premature budget exhaustion and interprets trigger dynamics as policy consolidation. Appendix B.4 strengthens the tentative cold-start interpretation into format alignment rather than teacher-strategy distillation. Existing limitations and failure conditions are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code/checkpoint access link and explains RLVMR trajectory provenance, teacher-generated reasoning and real-interaction collection within the existing 90/10 SFT recipe. V1's explicit '300 trajectories for each environment' wording and future SFT-data-release promise are omitted; this does not establish an actual dataset-size change.

R1.justification: New Appendix E.2 contrasts SPARK with ARPO, FR3E and DeepSearch. V2 also adds ATLAS/MAESTRO citations and removes the Sutton and Kimi Team references. The central positioning around intrinsic exploration signals remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: expanded and structured SFT explanations, new appendix subsections, acknowledgments, title/author formatting and equation punctuation. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds five compact tables: 5, 7, 9, 10 and 16. Existing tables are renumbered and repositioned, while all original figures and case-study displays are retained within the same two-column design.

improvement.justification: Clearer SFT provenance, code/checkpoint access information and targeted diagnostics improve transparency and support for design choices. The gain is limited: test-time compute and voting details are underspecified, and teacher similarity alone does not establish the stronger format-alignment interpretation. The central benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
